text: Thank you for the normal blood culture and electrolyte results; since your vomiting is bilious, we must urgently rule out a midgut obstruction. Have you noticed any abdominal distension, or did you pass your first meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding the meconium passage, which significantly lowers the likelihood of midgut volvulus. Given the history of bilious vomiting starting immediately after birth, a malrotation with midgut volvulus remains our top concern despite the normal initial labs. Please tell me if you have noticed any bilious material in your stool or if there is any abdominal tenderness to palpation?
